5+ years of experience in Mission Critical, Power Infrastructure, or Water Treatment preferred
Excellent problem-solving skills, with an adaptable and flexible style in working with different types of individuals
Strong understanding of engineering principles (HVAC, thermodynamics, heat transfer, process engineering)
Excellent communication and leadership skills
Highly entrepreneurial and self-motivated, with the ability to successfully work on own

When a transformer slips three weeks at the factory, a data hall slips three weeks at the site.
We're hiring a Supply Chain Delivery Manager to own that equipment from purchase order to dock.

You will be the site-facing supply chain lead for a regional portfolio of data center projects: tracking every OFE line item against the construction schedule, running factory and logistics escalations with OEMs, holding suppliers and general contractors accountable for delivery performance, and giving leadership a clear, converged picture of delivery risk across the portfolio.

Your job is to make sure equipment production and delivery are never the reason a site misses its ready-for-service date.
This is a senior individual-contributor role on the Compute DC Infrastructure team, working daily with Construction, Electrical and Mechanical Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Commissioning, and our general contractors and OEMs. It is not a category-management or negotiation role — Sourcing owns supplier strategy and commercial terms — and it is not a people-management role. The emphasis is execution: schedules, escalations, logistics, and site readiness.

Delivery planning and schedule integration
Own the end-to-end OFE delivery plan for each site in your portfolio: order placement, engineering submittal/approval milestones, production slots, FAT dates, ship dates, and required-on-site (ROS) dates, integrated with the GC's construction schedule.
Engage during preconstruction with Construction, Engineering, and the GC to set OFE delivery expectations, sequence equipment arrivals to the build, and identify schedule risk before POs are cut.
Lead OFE kickoff meetings at the site level with the GC and internal construction teams, establishing points of contact, delivery windows, receiving requirements, and escalation paths.
Maintain the single source of truth for OFE status across the portfolio — a live tracker of every line item, its milestone dates, and its risk rating.
Supplier execution and escalation
Run weekly delivery cadences with OEMs and integrators on open orders; verify production progress against committed slots rather than accepting reported dates at face value.
Act as the primary escalation point for factory slips, component shortages, FAT failures, and shipping delays; drive recovery plans (expedites, partial ships, resequencing, alternate sources) with Sourcing and Engineering.
Partner with Sourcing on corporate-level supplier escalations, bringing site-level schedule intelligence to commercial conversations.
Hold GC OFCI teams accountable for receiving, storage, and installation-readiness performance; manage the change/claim process when delivery issues affect the GC's schedule.
Logistics and site readiness
Plan and coordinate transportation for oversize/overweight and high-value equipment — carrier selection, route surveys, permits, crane and rigging coordination — with our logistics partners and the GC.
Manage laydown, staging, and interim storage decisions when site readiness and equipment arrival diverge; coordinate with Quality and Commissioning on receiving inspection and storage/preservation requirements.
Ensure equipment arrives complete — accessories, spares, documentation, and vendor startup support scheduled — so installation and commissioning are not delayed by missing pieces.
Risk management and reporting
Identify, triage, and report delivery risks across the portfolio; propose solutions and drive decisions to protect capacity milestones.
Establish and lead recurring Capacity Delivery Reviews giving leadership converged visibility into OFE delivery status and risk by site and by equipment category.
Track delivery KPIs — on-time-to-ROS, schedule drift by supplier and category, escalation cycle time, expedite spend — and use them to surface systemic issues.
Feed lessons learned back into Sourcing (lead-time assumptions, contract delivery terms, buffer strategy) and Construction (ROS sequencing) to improve the next program.

8–12+ years in supply chain delivery, equipment expediting, construction management, or infrastructure program management on large-scale, schedule-driven construction programs.
Hands-on experience delivering power and/or cooling equipment for mission-critical facilities — transformers, switchgear, generators, UPS, busway, chillers, CDUs, air handlers — and familiarity with how those OEMs actually build and ship.
You've managed cross-functional escalations across construction teams, suppliers, and internal partners, and you know when to expedite, when to resequence, and when to escalate commercially.
Comfortable reading and influencing construction schedules (P6 or MS Project) and tying equipment milestones to them.
Strong written and verbal communication — you can turn a messy delivery problem into a one-page recommendation for leadership.
Data-fluent: you build and maintain trackers and dashboards, and you'd rather look at the numbers than trust a status email.
Thrive with high autonomy in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment; you own outcomes, not just updates.
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Experience with hyperscale or AI data center construction and OFCI (owner-furnished, contractor-installed) delivery models.
Experience supporting multiple concurrent projects (5–10+) across a regional portfolio.
Working knowledge of FAT/SAT and commissioning workflows and how equipment documentation gates them.
Heavy-haul / project logistics experience, including international freight, customs, and Incoterms.
Technical understanding of data center electrical distribution and cooling system design.
Familiarity with ERP/procurement systems and analytics tools (SQL, Power BI/Tableau, Smartsheet/Procore).
PMP, CSCP, or similar certification.

Location: [San Francisco / hybrid, or remote US near the regional portfolio?]

Global Security plays a critical role in protecting Axon's people, facilities, operations, and reputation. As the Crisis Management Program Manager, you will build and lead the programs that enable the organization to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disruptive events.
Serving as the operational heartbeat and connective tissue across Global Security and key business partners; including Legal, HR, Workplace, Communications, IT, Manufacturing, and Executive Leadership, you will establish the frameworks, governance, and relationships that transform crisis management from a reactive function into a strategic enterprise capability.
This is a unique opportunity to build a program from the ground up, influence executive decision-making, and help shape the future of Global Security at one of the world's most innovative technology companies.

Build Axon's Preparedness Program
This role offers a unique opportunity to build a capability that will shape how Axon prepares for and responds to critical events around the world.

Working across Global Security and key business partners, you will design and mature the frameworks, governance, and operational standards that enable coordinated, confident decision-making when it matters most.

Success in this role will be measured not only by how effectively crises are managed, but by how well the organization is prepared before they occur.

Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for Axon's Crisis Management Program, ensuring it evolves alongside the company's global growth and operational complexity.
Design and maintain enterprise crisis management frameworks, governance, standards, and response methodologies that promote consistency across the organization.
Build and continuously refine crisis playbooks, decision support tools, and operational procedures that enable rapid, coordinated responses to a broad range of scenarios.
Champion a culture of preparedness by establishing sustainable processes that improve organizational readiness and strengthen enterprise resilience over time.
Lead Enterprise Crisis Coordination
When critical events occur, effective coordination becomes just as important as the response itself. In this role, you will provide the structure, leadership, and operational discipline that enable cross-functional teams to respond as one. By establishing clear decision-making frameworks, escalation protocols, and communication pathways, you will help ensure the right people are engaged at the right time with the information they need to make informed decisions.
Working alongside the GSOC, Physical Security, Threat Intelligence, Workplace, HR, Legal, Communications, IT, Manufacturing, and Executive Leadership, you will help orchestrate coordinated responses that minimize operational disruption, protect our people, and strengthen confidence across the organization.

Lead the coordination of cross-functional crisis response activities during significant security incidents and disruptive events.
Develop and maintain crisis activation procedures, escalation matrices, and decision-support frameworks that enable timely, consistent responses.
Facilitate Crisis Management Team (CMT) meetings, ensuring clear accountability, actionable decisions, and effective follow-through.
Prepare executive situation reports and operational updates that provide leaders with timely, accurate, and actionable information.
Coordinate post-incident reviews, capturing lessons learned and driving measurable improvements across the Crisis Management Program.
Strengthen Executive Decision-Making
During rapidly evolving situations, timely information and thoughtful coordination can significantly influence business outcomes. In this role, you will help transform complex, fast-moving events into clear, actionable intelligence that enables leaders to make informed decisions with confidence.

Working closely with the Crisis Management Team (CMT), GSOC, Threat Intelligence, and executive stakeholders, you will ensure decision-makers have the right information, at the right time, in the right format.

Develop executive briefing templates, situation reports, and decision-support tools that provide clarity during complex events.
Coordinate executive notification and escalation processes for significant incidents affecting people, operations, facilities, or reputation.
Partner with Global Security leadership to ensure executive communications remain timely, accurate, and aligned throughout an incident.
Support executive travel, strategic events, and other high-profile activities by integrating preparedness planning into broader security operations.
Continuously improve executive crisis support processes based on lessons learned and evolving business needs.
Build Trusted Partnerships Across Axon
Effective crisis management begins long before an incident occurs. Success in this role will depend on your ability to build trusted relationships across the organization, creating alignment before critical decisions need to be made. You'll become a recognized partner to leaders throughout Axon, helping departments understand how preparedness strengthens business continuity, supports operational excellence, and enables the company to respond with confidence during times of uncertainty.
Through collaboration, influence, and credibility, you'll strengthen Global Security's position as a trusted business partner while fostering a shared culture of preparedness across the enterprise.

Build trusted partnerships with leaders across Legal, HR, Workplace, IT, Manufacturing, Communications, GRC, Physical Security, GSOC, Threat Intelligence, and other business functions.
Facilitate cross-functional planning sessions that align roles, responsibilities, and response expectations before incidents occur.
Serve as the primary liaison for enterprise crisis preparedness initiatives, ensuring stakeholders remain informed, engaged, and aligned.
Promote preparedness through education, consultation, and relationship-building across the organization.
Represent Global Security in cross-functional meetings, projects, and strategic initiatives where crisis preparedness and organizational resilience are key considerations.
Advance Preparedness Through Technology & Innovation
Technology plays a critical role in enabling effective crisis management, but its true value lies in how it simplifies decision-making, strengthens situational awareness, and enhances organizational preparedness. In this role, you will continuously evaluate and improve the tools, processes, and technologies that support Axon's Crisis Management Program, ensuring they evolve alongside the company's growth and operational needs.

## Description de l'emploi ##
L'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) de la Direction générale de la cohésion sociale (DGCS), contribue à la réflexion et au pilotage de l'organisation des prestations sociales sur le territoire cantonal.

Elle analyse les besoins des différentes régions, coordonne les acteurs concernés et accompagne la mise en œuvre et l'évolution des dispositifs sociaux, en veillant à leur cohérence et à leur accessibilité pour la population.

Elle a également pour mission d'assurer une vision cohérente transverse pour le parc immobilier subventionné par la DGCS qui comprend notamment l'hébergement médico-social (EMS, EPSM, ESE) et les ateliers à vocation productive, soit environ 400 bâtiments gérés par 250 partenaires.
Afin de mener un projet ambitieux visant à établir une stratégie pour la mise aux normes énergétiques et d'adaptation aux conséquences du réchauffement climatique du parc immobilier de la structure socio-sanitaire, l'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) recherche **un·e Chef·fe de projet Plan climat.**
Pour de plus amples informations, veuillez consulter le cahier des charges en cliquant ici ou contacter Monsieur Mathieu Capcarrère, Conseiller stratégique, à l'adresse email: dgcs.recrutement@vd.ch
## Responsabilités ##
* Structurer et mettre en place de la phase 1 du projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois de 2ème génération œuvrant à faire un état des lieux du parc immobilier accueillant des populations vulnérables et subventionné par la DGCS.
* Piloter la phase 1 du projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois (EMPD 24 LEG 168) et en assurer l-avancement selon le calendrier prévu et l-enveloppe budgétaire dédiée.
* Conseiller, renseigner et appuyer les mandataires externes, les interlocuteur·trice·s internes, et les partenaires impliqués dans le projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois.
* Initier et piloter la phase 2 du projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois en définissant et mettant en œuvre un ou plusieurs projets pilotes liés à la transition énergétique, à la durabilité et au climat, sur la base des résultats et analyses de la phase 1.
* Coconstruire les réflexions avec l-équipe UOT sur les questions de transition énergétique, durabilité et climat, et être activement partie prenante aux réflexions collectives de l-équipe et du service sur ces thématiques.

Build AI-assisted workflows that expand what the teams around you can cover, and hold them to real standards: a defined task, a way to evaluate output quality, explicit human review gates on anything touching financial reporting, and documentation so someone else can run it

The ideal candidate is an agile, results-oriented financial and administrative professional with a proven track record of managing complex budgetary and resource allocation functions.

Executes the commander's vision on resource allocation in support of mission and installation operations, maintenance, and sustainment. Directly assists the commander in the flexible management of all administrative support program functions, anticipating organizational needs.

Administer programs serves as the primary source of information and proposes alternate approaches to management to more efficiently operate programs and comply with higher-echelon policies.

Knowledge of automated data processing concepts and systems capabilities to accomplish budget/funding tasks. Knowledge of administrative, personnel, and manpower regulations, operating procedures, and policies to support the organizational mission.

Skill in the application of methods and techniques (e.g., cost-benefit analysis, ZBB, amortization) to analyze and evaluate the effects of changes in program plans and funding. Skill in formulating, justifying, and/or executing assigned budgets/programs.

Bring a holistic view of the IT ecosystem to design and planning decisions, so solutions support our strategy and day to day operations.
Document and share knowledge so that processes and decisions are legible and repeatable by others, not dependent on any one person.

Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.
So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff.

Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place.

Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.
Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
Role
We’re looking for a Global Enablement Program Manager, who can bring to life the Afterpay and Cash App value propositions through our biggest channel: our people.

In this role, you will truly have the opportunity to manage a program that is mission critical to our organization's ability to scale, hit goals, and develop top talent.
This is a global role focused on North America, the UK and APAC. You may start the day sending out communications to the US team on recent business updates, followed by an end-of-day training session with the Australian team on a tool refresh.

s.h: You will develop a global enablement & training strategy that

Is a builder when it comes to AI, both building tools and supporting teams to ensure our teams are utilizing all the skills available to them, to be successful in their role.

Strategic agility: Proven ability to navigate highly matrixed, ambiguous enterprise organizations and build consensus among competing stakeholder priorities.
Process architecture: Deep experience building intake matrices, triage workflows, and operational playbooks from scratch.

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to join the AI Lab team at Doctolib.
This is an opportunity to become the person who makes a new European clinical AI research lab work, from the inside, at an early stage.
The AI Lab is tackling long-horizon, high-stakes questions at the intersection of clinical AI, patient modelling, causal inference, calibration, privacy, and real-world evaluation , with access to one of Europe's largest longitudinal EHR datasets.
You will be the operational backbone of a rapidly growing lab, combining research scientists, data scientists, research engineers, PhD students, and research affiliates. Your role is to build and manage the processes, interfaces, and infrastructure that let researchers focus on research, within a product company operating at European scale, with real patients and clinicians on the other side of every decision.

s.h: Your responsibilities include but are not limited to
s.t:
Own the operating model. Design and run the Lab's core processes from the ground up: portfolio management, roadmap tracking, async documentation, and decision-making cadence. Where a task recurs, build a process.
Connect research and product. Understand both the Lab's projects and product teams' roadmaps well enough to propose concrete collaborations and follow them through. Lead recurring interfaces such as the bi-annual DS-Research workshop and monthly research on-sites, with agendas set in advance and pre-reads produced and read before the meeting.
Filter and triage inbound. Manage partnership proposals, collaboration requests, and internal asks: answering or redirecting most, escalating only what merits researcher time.
Track dependencies to resolution. Own operational blockers (data access, compute, contracts, academic collaboration administration) and drive them to closure with the relevant teams. For example: run a CIFRE application through the university, the doctoral school, and the ANRT fast enough that the intern starts the PhD without a gap.
Run hiring logistics. Interface with Talent Acquisition to keep the pipeline moving: scheduling, candidate communication, process documentation, scorecard templates. Researchers keep the assessments.
Map the ecosystem. Maintain a live view of labs, companies, and institutions working on adjacent topics; prepare targeting decisions for partnerships, workshops, and data challenges. Lead the first data challenge end to end, from platform setup and legal clearance to participant communication.
Move information in both directions. Collect what the Lab needs from product, data, medical, legal, and people teams; report the Lab's scientific outputs, programme health, and critical risks to the company with clarity and precision.

s.h: You'll be a great fit if you
s.t:
Have at least 5 years of experience in programme management, research operations, or a comparable high-complexity role, ideally within an AI, engineering, scientific, or product environment
Have a demonstrated ability to design and run processes from scratch, coordinate multiple workstreams across specialist teams, and hold a portfolio of priorities, dependencies, risks, and milestones with rigour
Are able to influence senior stakeholders and expert teams without formal authority, and follow unresolved items until they are resolved
Communicate with clarity and economy: you can make complex topics actionable for non-technical audiences and precise for technical ones
Have enough understanding of machine learning to follow research discussions, judge which requests merit researcher time, and translate the team's goals for the rest of the company; deep domain expertise can be learned on the job
Are fluent in English; working French is required, as academic-administration processes (CIFRE, ANRT, doctoral schools) run in French

s.h: It would be fantastic if you
s.t:
Have operated as Chief of Staff to a CTO, VP Engineering, Research Director, or Head of AI, or as a Research Operations Manager in an AI lab, university, hospital, or industrial research organisation
Are familiar with academic-industry collaborations, CIFRE, PhD programmes, grants, or data challenges
Have experience with clinical AI, healthtech, model evaluation, AI safety, privacy, or data governance

Hey there!
We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.
Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.
Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.
Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?
To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!
Ready to be part of the experience?
Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.
As part of the Fever Originals team , you will use data and insights to create one-of-a-kind events and experiences that allow people to have unforgettable moments.
This position will support Fever Originals’ team. Your role will be to help the project manager with her daily tasks. This is an exciting opportunity to join the team at an early, high-growth stage and have ownership in creating new experiences.
The role requires a mix of business development and operational experience. Candidates need to be passionate about the entertainment and events industry. You will have to be comfortable delivering results in an ambiguous environment, being exceptionally detail-oriented while looking around corners, and think bigger about how we create a compelling experience.
This role requires flexibility, creativity, attention to detail, and the ability to meet deadlines while staying within budget .
Strong communication skills are critical to success in this role. The right candidate will be a self-starter and have strong interpersonal skills.
You can expect to join a group of diverse, hardworking team players, where a cultural fit is someone willing to stay humble, learn, and work nimbly. We welcome applications with unusual backgrounds with the expectation that the applicant will have acquired hard or soft skills and maturity throughout their experiences.

Participate in all aspects of event productions, including pre-production logistics planning, vendor selection, staff planning, onsite execution, as well as post-event wrap-up
Create productions timelines and ensure that teams are keeping to schedule
Communicate and collaborate with internal cross-functional teams and stakeholders to drive alignment and execution of event deliverables
Manage multiple productions and help scale Candlelight projects against team targets
Deep dive in budgets of different scales
Venue research and booking
Handle administrative duties including expense reports, invoicing, and working with the legal department on contracts

Strong fluency in German and English
Preferably having already an experience in the event production industry
Ability to manage multiple projects at any given time and pull together multiple aspects of a project in an organized and efficient way

Huge appetite for learning and the ability to pick up new skills quickly
You'll be solution-focused, identifying problem areas and then try to find solutions
Have strong communication skills and a proven track record of building positive working relationships
Able to communicate with partners, brands, agencies, and talent on efforts
Collaborative and willing to “get hands dirty”
Availability to travel
Starting date: September/October 2026

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!
As AI reshapes how products get designed and built, the systems that supply context - design systems, content, the relationships between design and code - are becoming some of the most consequential surfaces we work on.

We're looking for an experienced Design Program Manager to be the operational backbone of our new Context Platform pillar, helping Figma determine the future of leveraging organizational design context to go from idea to production. You'll own end-to-end design program management for the pillar and help define how a brand-new set of teams operate.
You'll be a right-hand partner to the pillar's Senior Design Director, working alongside design managers, ICs, TPMs, and XFN leaders across a set of deeply interconnected teams. As Context Platform underpins so much of the product, much of the work is cross-pillar: you'll be the person making sure dependencies surface early, decisions have clear owners, and designers across Figma know how to plug in.
This is a senior IC role suited to someone with high agency who is comfortable building in ambiguity - standing up processes quickly, seeing what sticks, and removing what doesn't.
This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

Own end-to-end design program management for Context Platform initiatives, including planning, prioritization, coordination, risk management, and communication across design & XFN partners
Partner closely with design leadership and engineering counterparts to keep design intent and technical execution aligned in a highly technical problem space
Define the operating model for a new pillar - the crits, design reviews, rhythms, and decision-making paths that help a nascent set of teams work well from the start
Orchestrate cross-pillar collaboration, making sure Context Platform work that touches other product surfaces is well sequenced and clearly owned
Define, pilot, and scale frameworks and rituals that make cross-team collaboration easier for designers - and evolve or retire them as needs change
Contribute to internal AI enablement for designers, partnering with DesignOps and developer experience teams on tooling, workflows, templates, and learning forums
Identify opportunities to streamline, automate, or remove operational overhead
Communicate progress, risks, tradeoffs, and dependencies clearly to design leadership and executive stakeholders

s.h: We'd love to hear from you if you have
s.t:
5+ years of experience in Design Program Management, DesignOps, or a related discipline
A track record of leading complex, fast-moving programs across design, product, and engineering
Deep understanding of design systems, how agents will consume design system context, and how to support designers' craft
Experience working on AI-powered products, internal AI enablement, or adjacent workflows
Technical curiosity and aptitude to partner fluently with engineering and design engineers

s.h: While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have
s.t:
Hands-on experience with automation, scripting, or AI orchestration tools to reduce operational overhead
Prior experience as a product designer or in a design-adjacent role

We are looking for an Immigration Program Manager to support Figma's growing Immigration and Global Mobility programs.
In this role you will serve as a primary point of contact for visa-sponsored Figmates, managing immigration cases and compliance while providing a high-touch employee experience. You'll also support international relocations and broader global mobility programs and get exposure to M&A and international expansion.
You'll partner closely with immigration counsel and teams across People, Finance, Legal, Talent Acquisition, and Payroll to improve our processes, resources, reporting, budgeting, vendor management, and program administration.
This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

Serve as primary contact for Figmates and stakeholders on immigration inquiries, visa assessments, case status, and strategy
Manage a high-volume immigration case portfolio - including permanent residence processes (PERM, I-140, AOS, ILR) — across US, EMEA, JAPAC, and LATAM
Coordinate with outside immigration counsel on case petition preparation, timelines, RFE responses, audits, and compliance matters
Track and proactively manage work authorization expirations across the foreign national population, ensuring timely renewals and escalations
Partner with People Partners and Talent Acquisition to assess immigration sponsorship feasibility for new hires and internal transfers
Develop and maintain Figmate-facing immigration resources, FAQs, playbooks, and compliance documentation (PAF, etc.), and design training for key stakeholders and Figmates globally
Monitor regulatory changes and manage internal reporting, trackers, dashboards, and I-9 compliance efforts, serving as internal POC for I-9 escalations
Coordinate international relocations and participate in global mobility, People M&A, and international expansion initiatives

s.h: We'd love to hear from you if you have
s.t:
5+ years of experience managing immigration for EMEA, APAC, and AMER at a global technology company or employment-based immigration law firm
Deep subject-matter expertise in U.S. nonimmigrant and immigrant visa categories (H-1B CAP & cap-exempt, L-1, O-1, TN, OPT, PERM, EB-1/EB-2, AOS, EADs)
Experience managing multiple vendors and supporting complex immigration matters, including international relocations and/or assignments
Experience with People Ops-related compliance projects, with interest in contributing beyond the immigration and global mobility functions
Exceptional project management, organizational, and prioritization skills, with the ability to translate complex legal concepts into crisp written and verbal communication

s.h: While it's not required, it's an added plus if you also have
s.t:
Experience supporting immigration needs related to M&A activity
Strong expertise in Singapore immigration and the COMPASS framework
Working knowledge of international assignment management, including assignment design, cost projections, tax equalization, and assignee lifecycle support
Familiarity with cross-border tax concepts - including hypo tax, shadow payroll, and equity income sourcing for mobile employees and expatriates — and equity income sourcing mechanics for RSUs and stock options
Experience managing business traveler compliance programs, including short-term assignment tracking and permanent establishment risk identification

Company Description
We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.
Job Description
At Olsson, we are passionate about improving communities through expert engineering and design. Our people are our greatest asset, and we are committed to creating an environment where you can grow, lead, and make an impact.
Our Data Center team delivers multidisciplinary engineering and design services for some of the world's most innovative companies. These projects represent some of the largest and most complex infrastructure developments in the country, creating opportunities to solve challenging problems, collaborate across disciplines, and shape the facilities that support global connectivity.
We are seeking a Construction Administration Project Manager to help guide large-scale data center projects through the construction phase. In this role, you will connect design intent with field execution, coordinate across multidisciplinary teams, and help keep construction-phase decisions, documentation, and deliverables moving forward.

You will build trusted relationships with clients and project partners while supporting quality, safety, schedule, and successful project closeout. This role supports construction administration across data center projects and includes travel to project sites as needed for observations, meetings, and project coordination.

Serve as a primary connection between Olsson's design team, client representatives, contractors, consultants, and other project stakeholders during construction.
Coordinate construction-phase documentation, including requests for information, shop drawings, submittals, substitution requests, design packages, and related project records.
Review documentation for cross-discipline coordination, completeness, quality, and alignment with the design intent and contract documents.
Evaluate design changes and field conditions, coordinate technical input from the appropriate disciplines , and help assess potential effects on scope, schedule, and budget.
Lead or participate in project meetings, communicate decisions and action items, and follow through with the design team and project partners.
Track project progress, outstanding items, risks, and upcoming milestones while maintaining accurate and organized records.
Support project financial management through invoice coordination, change management, and monitoring of project budgets and schedules.
Conduct site observations as needed to monitor progress, identify potential deficiencies, and communicate findings to the appropriate parties .
Coordinate the resolution of technical and site-specific issues to help minimize rework, delays, and disruptions.
Support project closeout, including punch-list activities, final testing and commissioning coordination, record documents, and final deliverables.

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

Bachelor's degree in Architecture , Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field. In lieu of a bachelor's degree, an associate degree with equivalent experience is required .
4+ years of experience within the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry with increasing project responsibilities.
2+ years of project management, construction management, or construction administration experience, which may be concurrent with overall project experience.
Understanding of engineering and design terminology, construction processes, contracts, project financials, and relevant codes.
Strong communication , organization, time management, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to build effective relationships, navigate challenging conversations, and resolve issues across project teams.
Experience with Microsoft Office and construction management platforms. Experience with Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Newforma, Smartsheet, or similar tools is beneficial.
Commitment to exceptional client service, quality, and safety.

The typical annual salary range for this role is as listed below. Compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience, and qualifications. Employees in this role may be eligible for our performance‑based bonus and merit increases.

Additional Information
Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

We are seeking a Project Manager to lead the Short Circuit, Coordination, and Arc Flash (SCCAF) process for complex data center projects. In this role, you will bring clients, contractors, and technical teams together around the information, decisions, and milestones needed to deliver coordinated electrical studies.

You will help move the work from kickoff through final reports and labels while supporting system reliability, personnel safety, and a smooth transition from design into construction.

Serve as the primary point of contact for SCCAF coordination among the client, general contractor, electrical contractor, and Olsson engineering team.
Lead the SCCAF process from project kickoff through final reports and labels, keeping the work aligned with construction milestones and project priorities.
Develop and maintain a detailed SCCAF schedule, adjusting it as project information, equipment data, and construction activities evolve.
Coordinate the flow of SCCAF information and deliverables, including requests for information, submittals, equipment data, settings, labels, study revisions, and final reports.
Track required inputs and follow up with project partners to address missing information, field discrepancies, late design changes, or other items that may affect progress.
Plan, lead, and document SCCAF coordination meetings while maintaining clear action items, responsibilities, and follow-up.
Partner with technical teams to support quality, consistency, and alignment between SCCAF deliverables and approved construction documents.
Identify schedule, coordination, and project delivery risks early and work with stakeholders to develop practical solutions.
Support project management activities, including deliverable tracking, document control, invoicing coordination, project reporting, and adherence to Olsson's quality processes.

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.

Dein Bewerbungsprozess

s.h: So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess bei uns ab
s.t:
Schritt 1: Online Bewerbung
Reiche deine Bewerbungsunterlagen online über unser Jobportal ein. Damit wir deine Unterlagen weiterbearbeiten können, musst du ein Login erstellen. Nachdem du deine Bewerbung eingereicht hast, erhältst du eine Bestätigung. Wir beurteilen jede Bewerbung individuell anhand der Kriterien im Stelleninserat. Das braucht manchmal etwas Zeit. Wenn deine Bewerbung passt, kontaktieren wir dich für ein erstes Gespräch.
Schritt 2: Gespräche
Im Vorstellungsgespräch - telefonisch, vor Ort oder online - möchten wir dich kennenlernen. Wir überprüfen, ob deine Erwartungen an die Stelle mit unseren übereinstimmen, welche Erfahrungen und Fähigkeiten du mitbringst, ob dich unsere Kultur anspricht und wie du ins Team passt. Bei beidseitigem Interesse und je nach Stelle finden mehrere Gespräche statt. Alle deine Fragen zur Stelle, zum Team oder zu den Anstellungsbedingungen sind immer willkommen.
Schritt 3: Weitere Schritte im Prozess
Je nach Stelle vereinbaren wir einen Probe- oder Schnuppertag, stellen dir eine fachliche Aufgabe, organisieren ein Treffen mit dem Team oder laden zu einem Assessment ein. In der Regel gehören auch Referenzauskünfte zu unserem Bewerbungsablauf. Über alle Schritte im Prozess wirst du transparent informiert.
Schritt 4: Bewerbungsentscheid
Du bist von uns überzeugt und wir von dir? Nach einer mündlichen Zusage erhältst du eine Bestätigung, die Vertragsunterlagen und Informationen, wie es bis zum Stellenantritt weitergeht. Es hat nicht geklappt? Wir freuen uns, wenn du dich trotz Absage auf andere spannende Stellen bewirbst.

## Company Description ##
**About Syngenta**
At Syngenta Crop Protection, we're pioneering solutions that safeguard global food security while championing sustainable agriculture. As a world market leader headquartered in Switzerland, we empower farmers with innovative crop protection technologies that defend against nature's toughest challenges.

We unite advanced science with digital solutions to develop intelligent crop protection that maximizes yields while minimizing environmental impact.

Join our mission of revolutionizing plant protection from seed to harvest. **Syngenta has been ranked as a-top employer-by Science Magazine and it has been awarded with the "Friendly Work Space" label to all its Swiss sites.**
## Job Description ##
At Syngenta, our goal is to build the most collaborative and trustworthy team in agriculture, providing top-quality seeds and innovative crop protection solutions that improve farmers' success. To support this mission, we are seeking a **Global Environmental Technology Lead**. This is a hybrid role based primarily in Muttenz, Switzerland, though Monthey can also be considered.
As Global Environmental Technology Lead, you will shape how Production & Supply identifies, develops and deploys the technologies that reduce environmental impact while protecting operational performance and our license to operate.

This is a high-impact global role for an accomplished scientist or engineer who can move confidently between technical depth, strategic direction and practical implementation. You will connect manufacturing sites, process development, environmental specialists and external partners to turn complex environmental challenges into scalable solutions.

* Set the global environmental technology strategy across waste, wastewater, air emissions, vent treatment, recovery and recycling, informed by Best Available Techniques (BAT).
* Identify, assess and mature emerging technologies, taking opportunities from laboratory and pilot-scale evidence through to robust manufacturing application.
* Partner with global and local manufacturing teams to solve critical environmental challenges, improve site performance and safeguard license to operate.
* Provide technical leadership and independent challenge for environmental projects, assessing feasibility, environmental benefit, risk, operability and cost.
* Influence product and process choices early by evaluating waste streams, especially wastewater, during active-ingredient process development.
* Develop practical, high-value solutions that reduce impacts to air, water and land across existing products and manufacturing sites.
* Build and lead a connected global environmental technology community spanning Technology & Engineering, Production & Supply, Environmental Managers, process development teams and external experts.
* Grow internal capabilities through technical coaching, knowledge exchange, training, literature reviews and partnerships with suppliers, consultants and technology providers.
* Translate complex environmental science and regulation into clear choices and decisive action for technical and business stakeholders.

* Master-s degree, or equivalent, in Chemistry, Chemical Process Engineering or a related discipline.
* Ideally 10+ years- experience in industrial chemical operations and/or process development.
* Demonstrated expertise in environmental technologies and a practical understanding of environmental legislation.
* Able to remain focused, resilient and effective in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
* Strong knowledge of waste, wastewater, emissions, recovery and recycling technologies.
* Solid grounding in organic and inorganic chemistry, chemical processes and process engineering; agrochemical production knowledge is an advantage.
* Working knowledge of environmental toxicity, chemical bio-transformation and environmental risk assessment.
* Proven ability to lead teams or workstreams in project, departmental or matrix environments.
* Experience in project and change management, with resilience in ambiguous environments.
* Strong analytical, conceptual, organisational and negotiation skills.
* Clear communication and stakeholder-influencing skills at all levels.
* Experience working across multicultural, multinational teams, with a recognised record of technical delivery.
* Fluent business English; French is highly advantageous.

* Kontrollieren der installierten Verkaufs-, Träger- und digitalen Preissysteme

* Einwandfreier Leumund
### Darauf kannst du dich freuen ###
* Befristete Anstellung für 4 bis 6 Monate, je nach Projektverlauf
* Verantwortungsvolle Aufgabe mit viel Eigenständigkeit und direkter Führung eines kleinen Montageteams

* Sorgfältige Einführung vor dem Projektstart
